# FDG9038

> DO throw an `OperationCanceledException` when aborting work due to a `CancellationToken`.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 9.2.5.1 Task.Status Consistency.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG9038
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: verified

Message: Throw an OperationCanceledException instead of returning when cancellation is requested in '{0}'

FDG9038 reports a return statement that is the whole branch of an if statement whose condition is the IsCancellationRequested property of a CancellationToken, in an async method, local function or lambda that returns a task-like type, as in the Bad example of the body. Loops that end when cancellation is requested, and other early exits, are not seen, so coverage is partial. CA2250 (use ThrowIfCancellationRequested) is not mapped: it reports the second Good example of the body, an explicit throw of OperationCanceledException, which the text allows (probe with SDK 10.0.402). There is no code fix.

## From the book

The Task execution engine handles `OperationCanceledException` and updates the Task to be in the `Canceled` state. Awaiting a Task in the `Canceled` state results in another `OperationCanceledException` being thrown, which normally results in a cascade that ends with program termination or a caller explicitly handling the `Canceled` state.

If you use the `CancellationToken.IsCancellationRequested` value to do an early return from a method created with the `async` keyword, then the Task for your method moves to the `RanToCompletion` state— not the `Canceled` state—and any caller awaiting the Task continues as if the method had completed successfully. This behavior is often a source of bugs.

The easiest way to ensure that the correct behaviors happen is to invoke the `ThrowIfCancellationRequested()` method on the `CancellationToken`, but manually throwing an instance of `OperationCanceledException` works as well.

```csharp
try {
  await SaveData(data, cancellationToken);
  QueueNotification("Data saved successfully!");
} catch (OperationCanceledException) {
  QueueNotification("Save was canceled.");
}
...

private async Task SaveData(
  byte[] data, CancellationToken cancellationToken) {

  // Bad: this causes the success message
  if (cancellationToken.IsCancellationRequested) {
    return;
  }

  // Good: this causes the canceled message for our caller
  if (cancellationToken.IsCancellationRequested) {
    throw new OperationCanceledException(cancellationToken);
  }

  // Good: this causes the canceled message for our caller
  cancellationToken.ThrowIfCancellationRequested();

  ...
 }
```
